chapters.summary: King Ahasuerus holds a lavish banquet to display his glory; when Queen Vashti defies his command she is deposed, setting the stage for Esther to become queen.
keyPoints: King Ahasuerus holds a banquet for the nobles in Shushan, displaying his abundant wealth and glory.
Queen Vashti refuses to come at the king's command, provoking him to furious anger.
The king heeds Memucan's counsel and issues a decree deposing the queen, in order to uphold a husband's authority.
chapters.application: When we face authority or conflict in life, let us act with wisdom and a humble, submissive heart, trusting that God reigns over all things and is preparing his plan.

chapters.summary: Esther is brought into the palace and becomes queen, and Mordecai also discovers and reports a plot to assassinate the king.
keyPoints: King Ahasuerus seeks a new queen, and Esther is brought into the palace and wins his favor.
Mordecai, who raised Esther, instructs her to keep her Jewish identity secret.
Mordecai discovers that two eunuchs are plotting to harm the king, tells Esther, and through her report to the king, the king's life is saved.
chapters.application: In the ordinary course of life, God is quietly arranging all things. Let us remain faithful in our duties, seize opportunities to do good, and trust that he will guide our lives.

chapters.summary: King Ahasuerus promotes Haman; because Mordecai refuses to bow to him, Haman plots to destroy the Jews and casts lots to set a date for the slaughter.
keyPoints: Haman is promoted by the king, and everyone bows before him except Mordecai.
When Haman learns that Mordecai is a Jew, he becomes enraged and plots to destroy Mordecai's entire people.
Haman casts Pur to choose a day, obtains the king's consent, and issues a decree to destroy the Jews.
chapters.application: When we face injustice and persecution, let us trust in the sovereignty of God; he watches over us in secret and will surely vindicate his people.

chapters.summary: Mordecai and the Jews mourn over Haman's decree of annihilation, and Esther, persuaded by Mordecai, resolves to approach the king in violation of the law to plead for her people.
keyPoints: Mordecai and the Jews put on sackcloth and ashes and wail bitterly over Haman's decree of annihilation.
Esther hesitates at first, but Mordecai reminds her of the responsibility and calling that come with being queen.
After fasting three days, Esther resolves to go to the king in violation of the law, saying, "If I perish, I perish."
chapters.application: When we face hardship, let us follow Esther's example: first seek God in prayer, and then courageously take up our responsibility, trusting that God will surely lead us.

chapters.summary: Esther risks her life to approach the king, who receives her with favor and accepts her invitation to two banquets together with Haman; Haman grows furious that Mordecai still will not bow to him.
keyPoints: After fasting, Esther risks her life to approach the king; he extends the golden scepter, and she finds favor.
Esther invites the king to bring Haman to a banquet, and the king agrees twice, showing his trust in her.
Haman is enraged that Mordecai will not bow to him, though the banquet leaves him feeling triumphant for the moment.
chapters.application: In times of hardship, let us follow Esther's example, acting with wisdom and courage, and trusting that God is secretly governing all things.

chapters.summary: This chapter tells how King Ahasuerus, unable to sleep one night, discovers that Mordecai's service has never been rewarded, while Haman, mistakenly assuming the king means to honor him, is instead forced to honor Mordecai — a foreshadowing of his downfall.
keyPoints: Unable to sleep, the king orders the chronicles to be read to him and discovers that Mordecai's service in saving his life was never rewarded.
Just as Haman is about to move against Mordecai, the king instead commands him to honor Mordecai.
Haman returns home, and his wife predicts his downfall, while Mordecai is honored.
chapters.application: Even when it seems you have been forgotten, God remembers your good deeds. Wait humbly, for his reward will come in its time, far beyond what you ask or imagine.

chapters.summary: At the second banquet Esther exposes Haman's plot; Haman is put to death, and the king's anger is appeased.
keyPoints: Esther bravely exposes Haman's plot, revealing the danger facing herself and her people.
King Ahasuerus is filled with fury, and Haman, terrified, falls before Esther's couch to beg for his life.
Haman is hanged on the very gallows he had prepared for Mordecai — his evil deeds return upon his own head.
chapters.application: In the face of injustice, let us speak up with courage and wisdom as Esther did, trusting that God will surely vindicate justice and bring the schemes of the wicked to nothing.

chapters.summary: Esther pleads with the king to revoke Haman's evil decree; Mordecai is promoted, and the Jews are delivered.
keyPoints: King Ahasuerus gives Haman's estate to Esther, and Mordecai is summoned and given the king's signet ring.
Weeping, Esther pleads with the king to revoke Haman's evil decree, and the king grants her request, issuing a new edict.
The new edict permits the Jews to gather on the thirteenth day of the month Adar to defend themselves and strike down their enemies.
chapters.application: In times of hardship, let us follow Esther's courage and wisdom, praying to God, seizing every opportunity to act justly, and trusting that he can turn any situation around.

chapters.summary: By God's mighty power the Jews turn defeat into victory, strike down their enemies, and establish the feast of Purim to commemorate God's deliverance.
keyPoints: On the thirteenth day of the month Adar the Jews gather and strike down those who hate them, but they take no plunder.
Esther asks the king to allow the Jews in Shushan one more day to continue against their enemies, and that Haman's ten sons be hanged.
The Jews establish the feast of Purim to celebrate their deliverance from their enemies and the peace they now enjoy, keeping it as a lasting custom for generations.
chapters.application: Let us remember God's deliverance in times of trouble, respond with gratitude and joy, and often share what he has done with family and friends.

chapters.summary: The achievements of King Ahasuerus and Mordecai are recorded; Mordecai is honored among the Jews, becoming a source of help and peace for his people.
keyPoints: King Ahasuerus levies tribute throughout the land, displaying his power.
Mordecai's achievements are recorded in the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia.
Mordecai holds a position of honor, seeking the welfare of his fellow Jews.
chapters.application: Whatever position we hold, let us be faithful in our duties; God will remember our good deeds and use us to bless others, bringing peace and joy.
